entries.note: Crossref abstract of Honigberg ASH 2007 (Blood 110:1592, 16 Nov 2007) has the quote verbatim; mouse probe occupancy public before any human dosing. Opener untested 2007, ibrutinib, oral correct.
Quote verbatim in Advani 2013 abstract. Pollyea ASH 2009 abstract (20 Nov 2009) reports 89% PBMC occupancy at 4 h in first cohort (2 MCL of 7), so year 2009 holds; direct readout, same.
Quote verbatim in Honigberg ASH 2007 abstract; occupancy readout stated before the phase 1, no human dose target yet. Untested opener 2007 correct.

Quote verbatim (Advani abstract). Year 2012 holds: Pollyea 2009 showed 89% (<90% target) at cohort 1 and the ASH 2010 Fowler abstract states no occupancy; full occupancy at 2.5 mg/kg first in JCO epub 2012-10-08.
Quote verbatim in Pollyea ASH 2009 abstract (20 Nov 2009), before the 8 Dec 2009 first MCL responses; canine opener 2009 untested, ibrutinib oral correct.
Quote verbatim (Wang 2013 NEJM abstract); ASH 2011 abstract (18 Nov 2011) verified: ORR 67% (16/24). Single-arm, primary ORR, response predicted and seen: same 2011 per single-arm rule.
Quote verbatim in Zhang 2017 CCR abstract; PDX first public 2017 after ibrutinib MCL results, so retro. Donors are mixed B-cell lymphomas incl. MCL; per-MCL pairs not read.
Quote verbatim in bundled 205552 PharmR text. Opener untested, proxy year 2009 from FIH start; ibrutinib oral correct.
Quote verbatim in bundled PharmR text ('increased platelet counts were seen in rats and dogs'); thrombocytopenia in MCL patients the animals reversed: contra, opposite.
Quote verbatim in Zhang 2025 Sci Adv abstract (epub 2025-12-05). Acalabrutinib monotherapy lead-in readout, combination_with null fits; untested opener not_measured.

Quote verbatim. Acalabrutinib cycle-1 monotherapy, combination_with null correct. Comparison is per-patient WBC kinetics in 4 patients, not AVO's primary endpoint; kept retro as a patient-level readout (see rule question).
Quote verbatim in Rahal 2014 abstract (epub 2013-12-22). Biomarker-selected (TRAF2/BIRC3) ibrutinib prediction, untested not_measured correct.

entries.rule: Status table (same needs the model's prediction to agree for a drug of this class) and evidence rule 5 untested_reason unsettled
entries.note: Freeman 2022 quote verbatim, but the BIRC3 effect is for the whole RAY cohort (ibrutinib and temsirolimus arms), not shown for ibrutinib alone: prognostic, not a test of ibrutinib insensitivity. Entry already carries untested_reason unsettled.
entries.adjudication_note: Status table: same needs agreement for a class drug; Freeman 2022 reports the BIRC3 effect across both RAY arms (incl. temsirolimus), not for ibrutinib alone. Rule 5: untested, unsettled (already set on draft).

entries.note: Quote verbatim in bundled 213217 MultidisciplineR text. Zanubrutinib is a member; opener untested unpublished, proxy 2014.

Quote verbatim. Contra holds on thrombocytopenia (R/R MCL 28%, animals raised platelets); AF basis is the pooled B-cell population (review: none or 1.6% in R/R MCL), so note should drop AF as an MCL harm.
Quote verbatim in bundled 210259 MultidisciplineR text. Acalabrutinib opener untested unpublished, proxy 2014 correct.
Quote verbatim in bundled 210259 text. Animals showed no platelet or bleeding signal; ACE-LY-004 bleeding and platelet decreases in MCL patients: contra stands.

Harrington 2016 quote verbatim (PLoS One epub 2016-07-19). Own acalabrutinib track on the canine model is right. Dog run post-dates ibrutinib MCL responses, so retrodiction could be true on the opener; no status effect.
Lancet abstract quote verbatim (epub 2017-12-11; label Oct 2017 also 2017). Single-arm ORR 81%, response as dogs showed; retro by post-dating ibrutinib MCL 2011, correct.
Quote verbatim in Pollyea ASH 2009 abstract; it shows the canine system in use for ibrutinib in 2009 (an efficacy sentence, adequate for an untested opener).

Patient quote verbatim in Wang ASH 2011 abstract. PNAS 2010 'well-tolerated' is not in the abstract (drafter read full text). Dog claim (Jul 2010) post-dates Pollyea 2009 'extremely well tolerated', so retro is right.
Harrington 2016 quote verbatim in abstract; passing tolerability claim is a scorable safety prediction; untested opener 2016 correct.
Lancet abstract quote verbatim. Dog tolerability (2016) post-dates ibrutinib MCL and acalabrutinib CLL tolerability, so retro; bleeding is scored on the tox track.

missing: Ex-vivo primary MCL/CLL cell buoyant-mass change vs in-vivo BTK inhibitor sensitivity, patient-level, comparison stated (Science Advances 2025, doi:10.1126/sciadv.ady2963, PMID 41348872): 'changes in cell buoyant mass within primary patient specimens ex vivo correlate with sensitivity to Bruton's tyrosine kinase inhibitors in vivo in MCL'. New track (ex_vivo, patient-level).

MCL cell-line pharmacogenomic profiling (Rahal 2014 Nat Med, doi:10.1038/nm.3435, PMID 24362935): ibrutinib-insensitive lines carry alternative NF-kB (TRAF2/BIRC3) lesions, found in 15% of 165 patients; a patient-level prediction of primary ibrutinib resistance. Track at least as untested/unsettled, or scored if a later patient-outcome paper tests TRAF2/BIRC3 vs response.

Acalabrutinib and zanubrutinib (members) have their own FDA nonclinical reviews (NDA 210259, 2017; NDA 213217, 2019) not in the bundle: dog/rat tox vs patient AF, bleeding and cytopenias should be checked as further safety entries on a tox track.

Acalabrutinib canine B-NHL (Harrington 2016, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0159607) and zanubrutinib occupancy (PBMC and lymph-node, Tam 2019 Blood) are in notes only; they would be member-drug entries on the existing canine and occupancy tracks, no status change.

Acalabrutinib rat/dog GLP toxicology and dog telemetry (NDA 210259 MultidisciplineR 2017, in bundle): 'acalabrutinib had no toxicologically-significant effects on cardiovascular function in a cardiovascular study in telemetered dogs', while label lists AF/flutter 3% and hemorrhage; would be a safety track parallel to the ibrutinib/zanubrutinib tox tracks (likely contra).

Acalabrutinib platelet-function models (light-transmission aggregometry and humanized VWF-HA1 mouse thrombus formation) predicted fewer platelet effects than ibrutinib (FDA NDA 210259 MultidisciplineR 2017, pharmacology section); compare ELEVATE-RR head-to-head bleeding/AF (Byrd 2021 JCO, doi:10.1200/JCO.21.01210, CLL, imported_from). A comparative-safety track not drafted.
rule_questions: registry_date when the trial registry has no results posted: the draft uses the first-posting date; rule 6 reads as results posting only, implying null. Which?

Safety year when the FDA review was signed 2013 (MCL approval Nov 2013, NDA 205552 Orig1) but the bundled copy sits in the 2014 Orig2 folder: does the year follow the earliest public posting of any copy of the review (possibly 2013 under Orig1)?
Is 'occupancy correlated with efficacy' in a mouse paper a model-stated dose target for the dose cell, or only an engagement prediction, given the brief bars targets the model never stated?
magnitude 'opposite' on a silence-contradicted harm where animals moved the lab value the other way (platelets rose): the brief defines 'opposite' for a predicted harm that never appeared.

Is a biomarker's pooled prognostic effect across a randomized trial's in-class and out-of-class arms (RAY: ibrutinib vs temsirolimus) admissible as a same for a model predicting in-class insensitivity, or untested?

Efficacy, patient-level models (efficacy 5): when a per-patient ex-vivo prediction is compared with per-patient sensitivity on a non-endpoint measure (cycle-1 WBC kinetics in AVO), does the primary-endpoint rule demote it to untested, or does a patient-level readout stand on its own?
